problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+4{z}^{2}},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ at the point $(3,-1,-2).$
worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the constant multiple and chain rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}) \\  & =y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}) \\  & =y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({({x}^{2}+4{z}^{2})}^{1/2}) \\  & =y\cdot (\frac{1}{2}{({x}^{2}+4{z}^{2})}^{-1/2})\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+4{z}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{y}{2\sqrt{{x}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+4{z}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the sum rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{2\sqrt{{x}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+4{z}^{2}) & =\frac{y}{2\sqrt{{x}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}}\cdot (\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{z}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{y}{2\sqrt{{x}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}}\cdot (2x+0) \\  & =\frac{xy}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(3,-1,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(3,-1,-2)} & =\frac{(3)(-1)}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+4(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{9+16}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{25}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
